items.title: Liquidation fade: the planned tests that were never run

forms.what: pessimistic fills (z=8 m=5 e=1): entry 1 / 2 / 5 min late, +30 and +50 bp slippage per side, no target fills in the first minute
forms.result: z8 d1: +194 bp at close, +129 1 min late, +106 2 min, +88 5 min (p .02); net of +30 bp/side +15..+56 but ex-top3 fails; 15 variants

forms.what: cascade-only: enter only when >= 5 coins have triggered (z>=6) in the previous 30 min, causal count over all coins with 1-min data
forms.result: dose in breadth: <5 coins ~0/neg, 10-19 +37, >=20 +97 (p .002); almost all triggers are cascades already; 6 variants

forms.what: wait for the end: first up-close minute after volume has fallen below half of the cascade's peak minute; compare adverse excursion
forms.result: waiting for volume to halve: +2.5 / +7.7 bp vs +105 / +194 for the reversal bar: the pattern is the edge, not the waiting; 2 variants

forms.what: perp discount: split by premium index at the low (archive premiumIndexKlines 1m)
forms.result: premium drop: deep tercile +105, none +11, but it proxies the size of the fall (no difference within fall terciles); big-fall tercile +260; 3 variants

forms.what: exits: author's two levels vs fixed 5/15/60/240 min vs trailing; no tuning beyond these
forms.result: longer is better: 5m +121, 15m +156, 60m +304, 4h +418 (p .003); author exit +194; 5 variants

forms.what: hedged: long the coin, short the same USD of BTC (is the bounce coin-specific or the market's?)
forms.result: hedged with BTC 15m: explore +96 (p .002); confirmT +97 (n 36, p .08), confirmC +14 (p .74, 2025 -266): not confirmed

forms.what: thin coins vs liquid coins (terciles of 30-d volume); where is the bounce largest after a volume-scaled cost?
forms.result: thin +24 (n.s.), mid +63, liquid +119 (z6, 1 min late): better on liquid coins; 3 variants

forms.what: climax within the last 5 minutes (largest-volume down minute), reversal bar later, as his chart shows
forms.result: d 1-5, 1 min late: explore +123 (p .002); confirmT +29 (p .30), confirmC +69 (n 1089, 221 d, p .04; vs same drops p .062), every year +; net -8 at +30 bp/side: not confirmed

items.reason: Real effect (pattern beats equal drops, null data ~0, every year + on 73 coins) but a taker entry after the close is too late and too dear: 30 bp worse fills kill it; misses the pre-registered bar. Untested: resting entries (T1), context (T2, T3), real liquidations (L2), live fills (E1).

items.title: Gap fill: next value forms where yesterday traded least

forms.what: overlap of today's value area with yesterday's least-traded third vs a random third of the same width [S1e: see form f, the source picture shows a valley between two humps; keep this form as the literal reading]
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, 10,919 coin-days, 1-min volume spread over 10-bp bins: next-day volume share in yesterday's least-traded third 17.2% vs 18.0% for the same bins mirrored around the next open (diff -0.86 pp, CI [-1.38, -0.35], every year -); most-traded third 26.5% vs 24.0% (+2.5 pp, p < .001, every year +). Dose runs the wrong way: thinnest tenth -0.51 pp, 2nd -0.16, 3rd -0.14. Claim reversed: tomorrow trades where yesterday traded MOST (volume memory), not in its gaps. Volume conservation check 1.0

forms.what: nearest low-volume node above/below the open: reached before the same distance the other way? placebo = node set of 8 days earlier
forms.result: 7,376 days with an interior LVN (smoothed local min <= 30% POC) near the open: reached before the same distance the other way 49.1% (random walk 50%); vs d-8 node placebo at the same distance 49.5% vs 48.7%, diff +0.8 pp CI [-1.5, +3.2], p .49. LVNs are not targets (as single prints in pass 2)

forms.what: delta gaps: price zones where yesterday's |delta|/volume was lowest, same test (needs M0 for BTC/ETH/SOL; 1-min taker split otherwise)
forms.result: 10,878 coin-days, 1-min taker split spread over 10-bp bins: next-day share in yesterday's lowest |delta|/volume third 20.9% vs mirror 19.8% (+1.1 pp, p .003), highest third +0.5 pp; but inside volume terciles the low-delta half minus the high-delta half is -0.25 pp (CI [-0.71, +0.23], p .28): the 'delta gap' pull is the volume-memory effect of form a, nothing of its own

forms.what: trade: breakout into a low-volume zone, target its far edge, stop the near edge; payoff vs random-walk odds
forms.result: no attraction to support a trade: low-volume zones are entered LESS than mirror zones (a, g), LVN first passage is 49-50% (b, g) and the same far-edge-before-near-edge geometry failed in pass 2 (single-print bands 48-49% vs placebo 51-52%). A target/stop trade on a 50% first passage has random-walk odds by construction

forms.what: law 5 'what doesn't happen' (wa 18.10.57(1)): low-volume gap approached >= 3 times in 5 days and NOT filled -> move away from it, vs gaps never approached
forms.result: untouched interior LVNs over 5 days, approach = hour within 30 bp (deepest node only: 24 events with >= 3 approaches, MDE 251 -> too few) and every node within 50 bp: 198 events, from day-5 close signed AWAY from the node: 24 h -20 bp vs matched (same 5-day move quintile, never approached) +26, diff -46 p .31, MDE 85; 72 h -38 vs +41, p .29. Direction is the opposite of 'move away'. 2 variants

forms.what: the gap in his picture (tg:29) is the VALLEY BETWEEN TWO HUMPS of yesterday's profile (bimodal day), not its thin tails: on bimodal days does next-day POC / value land in the valley, vs the same-width band elsewhere in the range and vs unimodal days; trade = enter at the valley edge, out at the far edge
forms.result: 4,692 bimodal days (two humps >= 30% POC, >= 15 bins apart, valley <= 50%): next-day share in the valley band 11.6% vs mirror 11.0%, +0.64 pp CI [-0.5, +1.9], p .29; dose wrong way: deep valleys +0.46 (p .76), shallow +0.65 (p .03). His picture (value forming in the valley between two humps) is not more common than the same-distance band elsewhere

forms.what: per-candle 'salad' profile (wa 18.10.31(2), S2p: 'where we had lots of volume, on next candle we have little ... pockets are magnets, flow has long memory and clustering'): 1h candles from aggTrades/1m bins (10-bp price bins), does hour t+1 put its volume into hour t's low-volume bins inside t's range more than a shuffled-bin placebo and a same-range random-day placebo? dose = LVN depth; trade view = touch of the nearest prior-hour LVN within 60 min vs same-distance placebo level
forms.result: hourly salad, 186,781 coin-hours: hour t+1 share in hour t's least-traded third -0.43 pp vs mirror (CI [-0.55, -0.33]), most-traded third +1.24 pp (every year); nearest prior-hour LVN reached before the mirror distance 49.99% (n 23,705). Pockets are avoided, not magnets: same volume memory as the daily profile

items.reason: 6 forms done + 1 skipped with reason. Volume memory, not gap fill: the next day (and hour) trades MORE where the prior traded most (+2.5 / +1.2 pp vs same-distance mirror bins, every year) and LESS in its thin zones (-0.9 / -0.4 pp, thinnest bins most avoided); bimodal valleys = mirror (+0.6 pp, p .29), LVNs reached 49-50% (random walk 50), delta gaps = volume, approached-not-filled nodes n.s. MDE 85 bp (24 h). Tested his literal reading, his picture (valley between humps) and his salad thread at 1 h.

items.title: The other balance laws, session profiles, poor lows, fat-node breaks

forms.what: edges reject until proven: first touch of a multi-day balance's edge from inside, vs placebo edge
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23: 3-day balances (common value band), day 4 opens inside, first touch of the composite high/low (median width 8.1%): back 0.25 w inside before 0.25 w beyond 43.1% (n 1,994; random walk 50%) vs 47.3% for the 8-days-earlier balance moved to today's price (n 2,158): diff -4.2 pp, p .035, MDE 4.2 pp; 60-min return back inside +2.0 bp vs +3.8 (p .68, MDE 15). Edges of a real balance BREAK more often than chance, the opposite of 'edges reject until proven'

forms.what: time/volume building at an edge -> break: >= 4 of 6 half-hours within 0.15 x width of the edge, then direction of the next move
forms.result: same 1,994 real touches by build (half-hours of the 6 before the touch closing within 0.15 w of the edge): reject 45.6 / 40.4 / 42.0 / 46.3 / 45.8% for build 0/1/2/3/4+ (placebo 47-50% flat): no dose; time building at the edge does not raise the break rate (if anything the most-built edges break least). r60 -8 bp at build 4+ (n 491) within noise

forms.what: destination of an imbalance = an older balance's POC (naked POC), vs placebo
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, 1,237 imbalance days (close beyond the prior 3 days' high/low) with a naked daily POC (last 30 d, untraded since) in the move direction (median 598 bp away): reached within 5 days 48.5% vs 53.3% for the same distance on the coin's other same-direction imbalance days without a naked POC near it: diff -4.8 pp, CI [-8.6, -1.0], p .02, MDE 5.5. Naked POCs are not destinations; if anything they are reached less

forms.what: 80% rule on session profiles and on 5-day composite balances (daily one failed)
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, open outside the prior value area, two 30-min closes back inside -> far edge vs stop 0.25 w beyond the near edge, out at session/day end. Counting only resolved trades (random-walk odds are conditional on resolution): session profiles 47.6% vs 49.5% RW (n 5,937, 22% unresolved, -2.0 pp p .02); previous day 37.2% vs 38.9% (n 2,448, -1.7 pp p .20); 5-day composite 21% vs 31% but 49% unresolved and a finite horizon favours the nearer stop, so not interpretable. The 80% rule is a random walk at best. BUG FOUND: pass 2 counted unresolved trades as misses against unconditional odds; its '26-30% vs 37%, t -8 to -11' was mostly that bias (corrected daily figure -1.7 pp, n.s.); verdict unchanged (no edge), numbers corrected in findings

forms.what: his exception: single-print band directly under a big POC should NOT fill; compare fill rates
forms.result: 8,820 previous-session single-print bands (10-bp rows, >= 3 rows, tails excluded), fill = far edge touched within 2 days: bands adjacent (<= 2 bins) to the session POC are rare (34); they fill MORE than distance-matched other bands (82% vs 72%, p .16; with a top-third POC 88% vs 69%, n 26, p .03, MDE 18 pp). His exception (should NOT fill) is not supported; too few events for more

forms.what: fat-node break (R41): close below the fattest node of a 20-day composite -> continuation vs an ordinary 20-day level break
forms.result: close through the 20-day composite POC (1,380 crossings) vs through the 20-day median close: next day +21 vs -15 bp (diff +36, p .044); but vs the 20-day node of 8 days earlier moved to today's price (n 1,481): +16 vs -22, diff +37 p .14, MDE 58; 3 days -9 bp vs placebo; 2023 negative, ex-top-3 +0.5 bp; dose wrong way (fattest third of nodes -4 bp, thinnest +38). No fat-node break continuation

forms.what: poor / empty low (R42): low made in one half-hour with no tail vs with a tail; retest rate within 5 days
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, 21,450 coin-day extremes, tail = bins from the extreme touched by one half-hour only: poor (flat, tail 0) lows retested within 5 days 74.6% vs tailed (>= 3 bins) lows at the same distance (ATR deciles) 74.9%, diff -0.4 pp p .84, MDE 4.3; highs 74.1 vs 74.0%. Retest rate flat by tail length (0-4 bins 72-76%). Poor lows are not special

forms.what: rotation factor ~0 sessions (R18): next-session range and direction vs R/F extremes
forms.result: 10,735 coin-days, daily rotation factor from 48 half-hours: R/F ~0 days (|RF| <= 3) next-day range 1.00 ATR vs 1.15 for |RF| >= 17, but inside today's range quintiles the |RF| quintiles differ by <= 0.1 ATR with no common slope (range is today's range, not R/F). Direction: next day against strong R/F -42 bp (top quintile, p .13, MDE 79), R/F ~0 +11 (p .35). Balanced (normal) days predict nothing

forms.what: time vs volume disagree (tg:49-50 'if its not the same then u have a fuckery brewing'): |TPO POC - volume POC| / value width -> next-day range and direction; placebo = random pair of days' POCs
forms.result: 10,725 coin-days, gap = |TPO POC - volume POC| / value width: no direction (top quintile next-day return toward the volume POC -2 bp, CI [-33, +29]); next-day range +0.12 ATR for the top vs bottom gap quintile (p < .001) but most of it is today's range: within today's range quintiles the top-gap days add +0.05/+0.02/-0.03/+0.02/+0.16 ATR (only the widest days). 'Fuckery brewing' = at most a weak volatility hint, no trade

forms.what: initial balance (first hour) high/low of each session, first touch later in the session, vs levels offset by 37% of IB width (tg:15)
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, 4 sessions/day, IB = first 60 min: 42,621 first later touches of IBH/IBL: back 0.25 IB-width inside before 0.25 beyond 48.2% vs 51.6% for placebo levels 0.37 IB-width outside the IB (n 36,936): diff -3.4 pp (p < .001, MDE 1.0); 30-min return inward -0.4 vs +1.2 bp (diff -1.6, p .05). IB edges are extended (broken) more often than arbitrary levels, never rejected; tiny either way (2 bp vs 13-bp cost)

forms.what: fat node + 'lower deviation' break with OI falling (wa 18.10.51: 'positions placed at the fattest side ... puked'): 1h close below 20-d node minus 1 value width -> speed of the next move, vs same break without a node
forms.result: 1-h close through the 20-d composite POC -/+ one composite value width (1,861 first crosses, 10 coins 2021-12..2023, 5-min OI): 4 h with the break +11.9 bp vs +18.6 for the same cross of the 20-d median -/+ width (diff -6.7, p .33, MDE 20); OI falling -5.2 (p .66), OI rising -7.5; 24 h -23 (p .26). His case (down break, OI falling) +4.6 bp CI [-23, +37], 2023 negative. A node adds nothing to a break

forms.what: single prints and tails at HIS resolution: session rows of ~4 bp (47 ticks at 57k), minimum 3 rows, tails kept apart (my pass-2 bands were >= 30 bp, so his typical ones were excluded)
forms.result: single prints at his resolution (4-bp rows, >= 3 rows, tails excluded; median band 40 bp wide, 118 bp from the session close): far edge before the same distance the other way 48.3% (n 13,399) vs 51.0% for the same band geometry 8 days earlier moved to today's price (n 12,828), diff -2.7 pp p .04, MDE 2.5. Same as pass 2 at 30 bp: real single prints are filled LESS than placebo bands

items.reason: 12/12 forms, explore COINS10 2021-23. Balance edges break more than placebo (reject 43 vs 47%, p .04), build-up has no dose; naked POCs reached less than the same distance (48.5 vs 53%, p .02); 80% rule = random walk (session 47.6 vs 49.5%, daily 37.2 vs 38.9% once unresolved trades are excluded; pass-2 numbers biased, corrected); poor lows = tailed lows (74.6 vs 74.9%); single prints under a POC fill more (n 34); 4-bp single prints fill less than placebo (48 vs 51%); fat-node breaks = median breaks (-7 bp, MDE 20), with OI falling too; IB edges extended more than placebo; R/F and TPO/volume POC gap only track today's range. Reason: profile levels carry no resting-order memory a day later; the only regularity is volume memory (P1) and that real levels get broken slightly more often

items.title: Composite and naked POCs as magnet and support

forms.what: naked daily POCs: probability of being touched within 5 days vs mirrored placebo distance
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, naked daily POCs (untouched the day after their day; median 507 bp away) touched within 5 days 54.8% vs 57.6% for the mirror level at the same distance (diff -2.7 pp, CI [-7.5, +1.5], n 3,352). Weekly POC 52.9 vs 53.6%, monthly POC 49.8 vs 59.0% (n 249). Naked POCs are not magnets

forms.what: 20-day composite POC as magnet: return toward it when price is 2-5 sigma away vs plain mean reversion
forms.result: days 2-5 daily sigmas from the 20-d composite POC (3,410): return toward it 1/3/5 d -37/-88/-91 bp vs days at the same sigma distance from the 20-d mean close (matched) -15/-99/-192; diffs -22/+11/+101 bp (p .34/.79/.09, MDE 59-111). Price moves AWAY from both (trend), the node no less than the mean; no magnet

forms.what: first touch of naked POC: bounce vs first touch of the daily open (his explicit comparison) and vs placebo
forms.result: first touch of a naked daily POC, 60-min return one bar late signed away from the approach: +15.2 bp (n 1,834) vs mirror first touches +3.1 (unmatched, p .17), vs side-matched mirror -7.6 (+23, p .02, MDE 19.5), vs side AND distance-quintile matched mirror -0.8 (+16, p .09, MDE 18.5); vs the daily open re-touch +8.5 (p .22). Dose: grows with distance travelled (+4/+10/+28 bp) and waiting time, SHRINKS with node fatness (+43/-4/+1 bp, thin to fat) = the opposite of 'defended volume'. Generic bounce after a long move; absolute +15 bp = one taker round trip. 4 baselines tried, not pre-registered

forms.what: weekly and monthly naked POC / VAH / VAL, HVN and LVN (his D/W/M overview templates have naked levels on; passes 1-2 only used daily): first touch vs placebo
forms.result: weekly and monthly naked POC/VAH/VAL (n 117-1,043): touch rates = mirror (weekly -0.6..+0.4 pp; monthly -9..-11 pp, n.s.); the large raw reaction gaps (weekly VAH -85, VAL +48, monthly VAL +203 bp) are an approach-side artifact (touches from above bounce up, touches from below keep rising in 2021-23); matched on side: weekly -15 bp (p .32, MDE 35), monthly +44 (p .40, MDE 139). Higher-timeframe levels are not special

items.reason: 4/4 forms, explore COINS10 2021-23. Naked daily/weekly/monthly POCs touched no more (daily -2.7 pp, monthly -9 pp) than mirror levels; 20-d composite POC no magnet vs the mean (price trends away from both); first touch of a daily naked POC +15 bp vs +(-1) for side- and distance-matched mirror touches (p .09, MDE 18.5) with dose growing in distance and SHRINKING in node fatness (generic dip bounce, not defended volume); weekly/monthly VAH/VAL reaction gaps were an approach-side artifact. MDE <= 26 bp in c

items.title: Weekend and CME: the collar price and the gap rules as he states them

forms.what: collar = Friday's highest-volume half-hour price after the US open; Sunday-evening entry toward it, out by Monday 17:00 NY
forms.result: collar touched more often than placebo (c16: 43% vs 29%, all 4 references, all gap sizes) but mean -20..+36 bp (p .5+): median +100, fat left tail; 2021 +50..+214, 2022-23 negative; BTC -67, ETH -14; 18 variants

forms.what: CME gap (Fri 17:00 -> Sun 18:00 NY) by size tercile: fill rate within 1/3/5 days vs a placebo gap at a random weekday 24-h-apart window
forms.result: CME gap: big gaps fill more than placebo (3%+: 48 vs 32% in 3 d) but toward-gap trade -26..-179 bp, small gaps same as placebo; 9 variants

forms.what: same for coins relative to BTC (excess gap)
forms.result: excess gap vs BTC hedged: -4..+6 bp, placebo -44..-77 (weekday excess moves continue); 3 variants

forms.what: Sunday pre-open bait: move 16:00-18:00 NY on rising vs falling volume (W3 itself belongs to the research session: do not repeat its walk-forward)
forms.result: bait fade: all -40..-131; rising volume +27..+65 (n.s.); LOW volume fade -156/-211/-535 (p .01/.04/.06), all years: it continues; placebo weekday opposite; 9 variants -> form f

forms.what: Monday US-open flow: first-hour taker imbalance 09:30-10:30 NY on Mondays -> rest of day / rest of week, vs other weekdays
forms.result: Monday first US hour imbalance to EOD +34 (p .04) but Tue-Fri +9..+33, diff n.s., falls with z; to Friday 0; 6 variants

forms.what: FOLLOW the Sunday 16-18 NY move when its volume is below the previous two hours' (found in explore d: it continues to Monday 17:00, dose-response)
forms.result: explore +156 (p .013); confirmT -7 (p .92), confirmC +36 (p .34, vs Thursdays p .05), 2024-25 negative: not confirmed

items.reason: Gravity is real (collar/gap touched 9-15 points more often than weekday placebo) but unpaid: fat left tail, only 2021 positive; every form MDE 80-200 bp, so underpowered rather than refuted. W3 (Sunday 12-18 fade) stays with the research session. Note for W3: fading works on rising volume only in explore, not confirmed.

items.title: Calendar claims, including the ones I called untestable

forms.what: lunar phase: new -> full vs full -> new moon returns (about 75 cycles since 2020; BTC and equal-weight top-30)
forms.result: lunar phase, explore 2021-23, 37 cycles: waxing minus waning -780 bp BTC (p .01), -881 EW30 (p .05), MDE 910 / 1,207 bp; the 2024-25 column (computed in the same call, seen) flips sign (+413 / +748). Sign flip between eras + MDE above the effect = noise; cannot be known with ~6 years of cycles

forms.what: quarterly expiry / equinox and monthly option expiry: week before vs after, vs other weeks
forms.result: explore days vs all other days: week before monthly Deribit expiry (last Friday) EW30 -0 bp/day (MDE 90), week after +52 (p .07, MDE 65); quarterly week before -22 (MDE 156), after +13; equinox +-3 d +25 (MDE 217). No pinning-then-release pattern

forms.what: turn of month, day of week, hour of week (one table, FDR inside it)
forms.result: one table, 176 cells (7 weekdays + turn of month on EW30 daily, 168 hours of week on BTC hourly 2021-23), BH-FDR 10%: 0 survivors. Largest: turn of month (last + first 3 days) EW30 +62 bp/day p .07 (MDE 83); best hour cells +-15 bp/h (Sat 00h, Thu 03h) at p .003-.03, expected from 168 tries

forms.what: FOMC and CPI days: drift 24 h before, reaction, reversal next day (dates from federalreserve.gov / bls.gov calendars, typed into the study)
forms.result: dates from federalreserve.gov and bls.gov (research/is3/C1_dates.json), explore: FOMC day before EW30 +122 bp vs other days (p .05, MDE 173), FOMC day +218 (p .06, MDE 325), day after -40; CPI day before -19, day -9, day after +55 (MDE 218-352). 24 FOMC / 36 CPI days: effects of +1-2% would be invisible; nothing significant

forms.what: September / Santa / Chinese New Year / sell in May: effect size and n only; verdict limited to 'cannot be known'
forms.result: explore: September -20 bp/day vs other days (MDE 131), Santa Dec 25-Jan 2 -15 (MDE 143), May-Oct -40 (p .17, MDE 63), CNY week before +208 (p .03, 3 events, MDE 258), week after +161 (p .07). 3 years = 3 observations of each season: cannot be known, as stated in the form

forms.what: Stock Trader's Almanac rules that transfer (pre-holiday, triple-witching week, first days of month): take from the PDF text
forms.result: Almanac transfers, explore: last US trading day before a holiday (incl. Good Friday) EW30 +160 bp (p .07, MDE 245, BTC +31); triple-witching week Mon-Fri -19 (MDE 178); week after triple witching +48 (MDE 215). Nothing beyond noise

forms.what: Almanac p120: a down Friday followed by a down Monday marks an inflection (lower over the next weeks), vs down Friday / up Monday and vs any two down days of equal size; BTC and equal-weight top-30
forms.result: down Friday + down Monday, forward 5 / 20 days vs any two consecutive down days of matched size (quintiles): explore BTC f5 +163 bp, diff +240 (p .06), f20 diff +265 (p .36); EW30 f5 diff +159 (p .54), f20 -33. The Almanac says LOWER after; crypto is, if anything, higher (bounce). Later column (seen in the same print) does not repeat (-77 / +151)

forms.what: Almanac p175 tax-loss 'free lunch': coins within 5% of their 52-week low on Dec 15 -> until Feb 15 vs the rest (cross-section, clean bnall); placebo = the same on the 15th of every other month; only 5-6 Decembers, so report effect and MDE, verdict limited
forms.result: tax-loss 'free lunch' (coins within 5% of their 52-week low on Dec 15, top-100 clean bnall, to Feb 15, minus the rest): only 2 Decembers had >= 3 such coins (2022 -604 bp, 2025 -1,371): near-low coins did WORSE; other months -348 +- 989 bp; MDE for 2 Decembers 1,959 bp. Cannot be known; the 2 observations point the other way

forms.what: Almanac p139, p226: FIRST day of the month (12x an average day) and last + first four days; split C1c into these two exact windows before looking at the table
forms.result: split before looking: first day of month EW30 +127 bp vs other days (p .05, MDE 176; BTC +64 p .24); last + first four days +64 (p .05, MDE 80; BTC +23). Almanac's '12x an average day' not seen with power; both below their MDE

items.reason: 9/9 forms, explore 2021-23, BTC and EW top-30. No calendar tag reaches significance after the 176-cell FDR or exceeds its MDE: FOMC day before/day +122/+218 bp (p .05-.06, MDE 173/325), first day of month +127 (MDE 176), turn of month +62 (MDE 83), pre-US-holiday +160 (MDE 245); lunar flips sign between eras; down Fri/down Mon is followed by bounces, not the Almanac's decline; tax-loss lows did worse in the 2 usable Decembers. OPEN by the MDE rule (daily effects of 1-2% on ~30 event days are invisible), practically nothing to trade or filter on

items.title: Kill zones, CME break hour, illiquid-hour moves, time-of-day flow

forms.what: kill-zone persistence: trend that leaves London/NY zones -> next zone, vs the same-length window at random hours
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23 weekdays, NY clock: sign of the London zone (02-05 NY) x NY zone (07-10 NY) return -6.1 bp vs +1.3 for every 3-h window x the 3-h window 2 h later (diff -7.4, p .18, MDE 13.6). No kill-zone continuation (if anything the NY zone reverses London)

forms.what: filler hours given back: move made between zones reverses in the next zone? [S1e tg:69: what it returns to is the previous session's highest-volume price, so target = that POC]
forms.result: filler (05-07 NY) given back in the NY zone: +0.2 bp vs placebo reversal -1.3 (diff +1.5, p .82, MDE 13.7); the London zone's busiest 5-min price reached before the mirror distance in the NY zone 49.0% (n 6,007, CI -2.9..+0.9 pp vs 50). Filler is not filled back toward the session's collar

forms.what: CME break hour drift (17-18 NY, t 2.3-3.6 in 2 coins): all 83 coins, year by year [S1e wa 18.11.01(2): his list has TWO windows, 16:15-16:30 NY (old equity-index halt, gone since 2021) and 17:00-18:00 NY; test both, the first only before its end]
forms.result: 17-18 NY hour +6.8 bp vs +2.2 for other hours (diff +4.6, p .22, MDE 8.8), all 10 coins positive but the years decay: 2021 +18.5, 2022 +2.1, 2023 -0.3. 16:15-16:30 NY (until the halt ended 2021-06-25): +0.3 bp (n 1,250). items.title: Oscillators: pinned extremes mean trend

forms.what: dip to 70 that holds = re-entry (his chart), mirror for 30

The reset to 50 is followed by the trend resuming (his own 'uptrend: buy the dip that turns up' template), not a reversal. items.title: The author's own indicators (guides never turned into rules)
items.src: R30; tg:90, 99, 100; pdf Crayons V3.4 (31 p), FSVZO V2.8 (16 p)

forms.result: fade the first 2 bars after a MACD(12,26,9) cross: 1h up-cross -0.4 bp diff vs matched (n 10,153, MDE 7.5), down-cross +2.0 (MDE 7.0); 4h -12/-4 (MDE 24-28); 1d -46/-27 (n.s.). Nothing at 2 bars; at 6 h the up-cross fade loses 8 bp (p .05)

forms.what: Leledc exhaustion bars (public script logic) at 1h/4h/1d
forms.result: Leledc exhaustion (close > close[4] count > 6, then an opposite bar at the 30-bar extreme): 1h bear +6.7 vs matched (p .48), bull -25.6 (p .20); 4h -22/+12 (n.s., MDE 117-219); 1d bear -321 bp (p .01, MDE 309: price keeps RISING after a bearish exhaustion bar, i.e. the signal is wrong-way), bull +169 (p .34). forms.what: FSVZO: volume zone oscillator with Fourier smoothing; enter on the first bar WITHOUT an extreme alert; midline as support [S1b: VZO14, alert = inside +-60/85/105 (dose), entry = close of first alert-free bar, exit at midline hold/fail; proxy smoothing fixed before the run]
forms.result: end of a VZO alert run (FSVZO proxy = WMA4 of VZO14), dose X = 40/60/80: after abnormal selling ends, long: 1h -16 (p .03) / -44 (p .007) / +36 (n 61) bp vs matched - the bounce he expects goes the other way, worse at stronger alerts; after abnormal buying ends, short: 1h ... -129 at X 80 (n 100); 4h/1d n.s. (MDE 72-513). The end of abnormal flow is followed by MORE of the same direction (flow persistence), not exhaustion

forms.what: Crayons: bearish / bullish climax, dominance shift, invalidation lines, only labels whose definition the guide gives [S1b: climax = pause OR reversal by trend age, base-trend veto; invalidation in form k]
forms.result: the Crayons guide (pages 14-17, opened in data/chat_extract/out/pdf/InSilico_Crayons_Product_Guide.md) defines climax points only in words ('extremely early reversal detection mechanics', 'in strong trends more often a pitstop marker'), no formula; the indicator is closed-source. forms.what: Fisher transform turns on 1-min (his original method), with costs

items.title: Tape behaviour: swings, streaks, change of character, VWAP, shakeouts

forms.what: successive swings: each up-swing smaller / slower than the last (zigzag 2 x ATR) -> trend weakening?
forms.result: zigzag (2 x ATR14) on COINS10 1h/4h closes 2021-23, at each confirmed swing: fade after a weaker (smaller) last swing vs after a stronger one: 1h 6 bars +4.4 bp vs -10.2 (diff +14.7, p .002, MDE 7.2; smaller AND slower +12.2, p .004), 24 bars +9 (n.s.); slower alone +3.4 (n.s.); 4h +20..+47 (n.s., MDE 30-77). His reading is right in direction (a shrinking swing marks a weaker trend: the counter-trade stops losing) but the counter-trade itself makes +4-6 bp gross: a FEATURE for trend books (with j's failed extension, F2), not a trade

items.title: Filter harness: does a signal improve a book that already works?
items.src: design.md §4 (filters)

forms.what: research/studies/is3_filter.py: book daily weights x coin-day or day mask -> SR / mdd / turnover difference with block bootstrap, explore <= 2023, confirm 2024-25; known-answer tests
forms.result: research/studies/is3_filter.py: book weights x coin-day/day mask (side-specific option), re-run through kripto.backtest with its slippage and funding; SR/ann/mdd per sample, paired 20-day block bootstrap of the daily diff. tests/test_is3_filter.py: identity, random-mask invariants, oracle wins / random does not, side masks. Real book (flow, bnall 1d, explore): look-ahead oracle SR 1.58 -> 21.3, 100th pct of random masks, passes

forms.what: baseline: 200 random masks with the same on-share and persistence (a filter must beat those)
forms.result: 200 random masks per filter, each coin's mask circularly shifted (same on-share and run lengths); pass = dSR > 0 and >= 95th percentile. Real flow book: a random 80%-on mask in 10-day runs cut mdd -23.5% -> -16.4% and SR 1.58 -> 1.62 yet sits at the 87th percentile (p daily diff .82): does not pass. Random masks' median dSR -0.24 (cutting names costs Sharpe). One judge = 201 backtests, ~4.5 min, 0.56 GB on bnall daily

items.reason: tool item, no hypothesis: harness built and verified on known answers (oracle passes, random fails; a random mask alone cut the drawdown by 7 points, which is why every filter is judged against 200 same-share same-persistence masks). Verdicts belong to F1/F2/X1

forms.result: F0 harness, bnall 1d explore 2021-23, block shorts after a cascade day (cross-sectional median day return <= thr): pre-set main variant (-7%, 2 days) flow dSR +0.05 (72nd pct of 200), xsmom +0.09 (73rd): fails. The bounce is a one-day effect (median coin +179 bp the next day), day 2 gives it back -> form g added and tested separately

forms.what: no new longs in 20-day highs made on a volume spike (R8)
forms.result: F0 harness, bnall 1d explore 2021-23: blocking longs in coins at a 20-day high on volume >= 2/3/5x the 20-day median COSTS both books: flow SR 1.58 -> 0.89/1.08/1.32, xsmom 1.19 -> 0.47/0.70/(5x pending), 0th percentile of random masks, dose monotone (bigger spike threshold = less harm). forms.what: oscillator-pinned names: keep / never fade (R29)
forms.result: R29 never fade a pinned oscillator, F0 harness, bnall 1d explore: block shorts while RSI14 >= 70: flow dSR +0.07 (70th pct), xsmom -0.05 (26th); >= 80 flow +0.07 (96th of 50, touches 0.6% of weight), xsmom -0.04; block longs while RSI <= 30: flow -0.13, xsmom -0.05; <= 20 flow +0.26 (96th of 50, touches 0.1% of weight), xsmom +0.01. Main variants fail in both books, the two flow 'passes' touch almost nothing and do not replicate on xsmom: the books rarely fade pinned names anyway. DEAD form

forms.what: P5: entries at prior POC / inside value vs outside
forms.result: F0 harness, bnall 1d explore 2021-23, day profiles from bn100 1h (650 coins, 100% of book weight covered): e1 block positions against location (long < VAL, short > VAH) COSTS flow -1.33 / xsmom -0.70 SR (0th pct, every year; VA 50/85 the same): mechanical, blocking = selling right after a late dump and missing the plain next-day reversal (form h); e2 block positions inside value: flow -0.98 (53rd pct), xsmom -2.16 (0th); e3 Dalton's responsive reading (block longs above VAH / shorts below VAL): xsmom +0.10 (97th pct of 100) but 2021 -0.30 and flow -0.26 (37th) -> fails the pre-set rule (both books, every year). 7 judges per book. Value-area location does not improve either book. DEAD form

forms.what: round-number and poor-low proximity
forms.result: F0 harness, both books, explore: f1 R26 block shorts within 1/2/3% below the next 1/2/5x10^k level: dSR +0.02..+0.06 / -0.01..+0.06 (40-73rd pct), touches 0.5-1.7% of weight; f2 poor (unfinished) extremes: block longs with a poor day low flow -0.83 (72nd pct), xsmom -0.77 (34th); shorts with a poor day high -0.07 (67th) / -0.46 (4th). Round numbers touch almost nothing; poor extremes = random masks. DEAD form

forms.what: cascade-day short block with a 1-day window (seen in b: 1 d +0.56 SR at the 100th pct, 2-3 d nothing): threshold dose -5/-7/-10% at 1 d, per-year dSR, both books; the bounce is the liquidation fade, so this is the book-level version of E1
forms.result: 1-day short block after a cascade day (median coin <= -7%): explore 2021-23 flow SR 1.58 -> 2.14 (100th pct, p .005), xsmom 1.19 -> 1.62 (99.5th of 200, p .009), every year + in both; -5% also + (flow 97th pct). Pre-registered; confirmT 2024-25 FAILS both: flow 0.82 -> 0.57 (dSR -0.25, 26th pct), xsmom 1.57 -> 1.25 (-0.32, 22nd), every year negative, mdd worse. Diagnosis: the next-day bounce after cascade days was a 2020-23 regime (mean next-day median coin +291/+106/+61/+153 bp) and reversed in 2024-25 (-28/-150 bp, 43-50% up days): cascades kept falling the next day. Vault not opened (the diagnosis table also printed 2026: 7 days, +228 bp; not used)

forms.what: seen in e1: flow's positions AGAINST the day's value location (long closing below VAL, short above VAH) are its best (blocking them costs 1.3 SR, 0th pct). Standalone test: next-day simple return of liquid bnall half-0 coins by close location vs the day's own VA (below VAL / inside / above VAH, distance in VA widths as dose), MATCHED on the coin's day-return decile, so plain 1-day reversal does not count; explore 2021-23
forms.result: standalone, bnall half-0 liquid coin-days 2021-23 (58,894, 123 coins, bn100 1h day profiles): close below the day's 70% VA by > 0.2 widths -> long next day +49 bp raw but +4 vs inside-VA days of the same coin and day-return decile (p .92, MDE 90); above VAH -> short -11 bp, diff -45 (p .14: above-value closes CONTINUE a little); dose table vs return decile flat (-1..+25 bp below VAL, +21/+27/-2/+202(n 301) above), years mixed. Location adds nothing beyond the plain 1-day reversal of the day's return. Diagnosis of e1's -1.33 SR: blocking a long that closed below value = selling right after the dump and missing the ordinary next-day reversal, not a value effect. DEAD form

items.reason: 8 filter forms on flow / xsmom (bnall 1d, F0 harness vs 200 random masks): size-bucket breadth, cascade-day short block (2 / 1 day), volume-spike highs, pinned RSI, value-area location (3 readings), round numbers, poor extremes, value-location reversal standalone. forms.what: feature vector at each example (about 25 features: fall, speed, volume decay, retrace of the first 1/2/3 min, taker share, trade count, location vs prior-day / week / POC, hour, trend, breadth, premium, OI) vs all similar moments: which unstated features are extreme in ALL his examples?

Only the MAGNITUDE (min bucket delta share) can carry M4e: extreme only on 2021-11-26 (6th pct). Stay-out day 2021-09-21 had the fewest negative buckets (5, 6th pct) and still rallied. Minute examples (4, 3 different families) not pooled: too few per family. Exploration on full sample, not a test

TSize, +-5 d excluded) long 3 d: +79 bp vs matched same-coin same-ret-decile down days +74 bp, diff +6 bp (p 0.98), MDE 353 bp, ex-top3 -54 bp, 2022 -13 bp. items.src: tg:167 'can determine how strong the bounce or dive will be from initial mechanical spring after liqs'; owner 2026-11-22

forms.what: features as T2b on every climax event (about 800k rows in data/is3/lshock.parquet); ridge and small gradient-boosted trees, walk-forward by quarter with a 1-day purge, trained on explore coins only
forms.result: ridge (numpy; trees not installed, so untried), 22 features incl. spring, side interactions, hour, dv30, breadth; walk-forward by quarter, 1-d purge, COINS10 explore, 62,928 climaxes, target 60-min fade return: OOS rank IC +0.075 (t 3.2, 7/8 quarters > 0); top-10% |pred| traded by sign +34.8 bp/event. But it is the known side rule: model agrees with 'fade dumps, ride pumps' on 78% of those events, the rule earns +33.1 bp on the same events, and vs the rule on matched climaxes the model is -7.5 bp (p .72, MDE 60). Taker-net +22 bp, p .099, 2022 +21 / 2023 +61, ex-top3 +7. Verdict: no information beyond side + volatility

forms.what: spring strength: retrace fraction and speed in the first 1-3 minutes, as a continuous predictor (dose-response curves with CIs), in both directions (weak spring = dive continues: short)
forms.result: explore (COINS10 2021-23), 63,322 climaxes (lshock 'any', both directions), spring = share of the 10-min origin->extreme move taken back by climax+3: dose-response is FLAT, not monotone: 60-min fade return +7..+13 bp in spring deciles 1-9 (weak spring does NOT mean the dive continues: bottom decile continuation card -13 bp, diff vs matched -1 bp, p .85, MDE 24), and turns NEGATIVE in the top decile (>54% retraced): -5 bp vs matched +6, diff -11 bp (p .022, MDE 12.5) = a strong spring means the bounce is used up, opposite of tg:167. All below taker costs (13 bp). Pump fades lose, dump fades win (as L1). Causal by construction (decision at the close of climax+3); trigger table passed null/causality in L1. Variants tried: 1 (spring at +3 min; spring1 stored, not scored)

forms.what: size the bet by the predicted return (top decile only / proportional) vs the fixed rule
forms.result: sizing on the walk-forward predictions (all OOS climaxes): fixed side rule equal size +6.3 bp/event (per-day t 1.66); proportional to prediction +28.4 (t 1.81); the SAME side rule sized by |prediction| +28.1 (t 1.78): the per-event gain is bigger bets on volatile events, not better direction; risk-adjusted no improvement

forms.what: shuffle test: same pipeline with permuted targets must earn nothing
forms.result: shuffle test, 20 permutations of the target inside every training window, same pipeline: OOS IC -0.0025 (sd 0.015), top-10% +3.6 bp (sd 7.8) vs real +0.075 / +34.8: the pipeline itself does not manufacture edge; the real model's edge is real but = the side rule (form a)

items.reason: 4 forms, none positive against its baseline in explore: (b) spring is not a dose-response (flat +7..+13 bp in deciles 1-9, top decile -11 bp vs matched, p .02, MDE 12.5 = a strong spring means the bounce is used up, opposite of tg:167; weak spring does not mean continuation, -1 bp vs matched); (a) ridge context model has OOS IC +0.075 (t 3.2, shuffle 0) but only reproduces 'fade dumps, ride pumps' (-7.5 bp vs that rule, 78% agreement); (c) sizing by prediction = sizing by volatility; (d) shuffle clean. Diagnosis: the state of a climax carries direction (side) and scale (volatility), both already known from L1; nothing about bounce strength. Untried angle: nonlinear trees (not installed; deciles in b cover the main nonlinearity)

items.title: 1-minute bounces and continuations in general (not only liquidations), by context

forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, 116,417 one-minute moves >= 3 sigma (no volume filter), one per coin per 15 min, decision one bar late: fade +1.4 bp (15 min) / +2.0 bp (60 min) overall. 10 context features x 10 deciles: no curve moves the 60-min fade beyond taker costs; only monotone one = distance to a round number (rho -0.85, but 5 bp end to end); extreme cells: 24-h trend top decile (move with a >7% trend) +17 bp [9, 25] and moves > 23 sigma beyond the prior-day extreme +12 [5, 19], each 1 of 100 cells, no dose-response -> not pre-registered. forms.result: explore 994 up-minutes z>=8 breadth>=2 (breadth cut seen first, said in prereg), long 60 min one bar late: +27.2 vs base -2.2 (p .002), dose in z (+10/+18/+21 at 5/8/12) and breadth. confirmC 7,030 on 73 coins: +46.9 vs +0.1, p .009, every year +; confirmT 559: +39.2 vs +2.5, diff +36.7, p .075 (MDE 59) -> FAILS the time card, vault not opened. forms.what: effort without result (wa 18.10.24(2), second example: the volume spike had a SMALL body, not a dump): 1-min volume >= 10x median with range <= median at a local low after a decline, then a small-volume opposite bar; vs same volume with a large range
forms.result: explore COINS10 2021-23, 31,856 volume >= 10x 24-h median bars at a 60-min low after a decline (+26,700 mirror at highs), fade one bar late. Claim REVERSED: 60-min long return rises with the bar's range (rho +0.88; rr deciles +2 .. +17 bp; 240 min +4 .. +27). His bar (lowest 2 rr deciles) +1.8 bp vs +17.7 for same-volume large-range bars (p .001, MDE 4.9); with his confirmation (next bar opposite, volume < 0.5x) +0.5 vs +17.3, and confirmation lowers the fade overall (+3.5 vs +8.4). items.title: Alpha-decay curve of the live books' trades (cost of a late run, best execution hour)

forms.result: Signed return of each daily target change from the 04:00 decision close, bp per unit |dw| (day-bootstrap CI), 4h known-answer check corr 1.00 (first run had a fillna(0) bug = fake changes, fixed). BN 82-coin 2020-26: +1h/+4h/+24h/+48h blend +0.6/-0.3/+2.3/+5.5, tsmom -0.5/-0.7/+7.0/+9.6, xsmom +1.3 (CI .5-2.2)/+1.2/+4.9/+9.7, carry +0.6/+0.7/+1.7/+2.6, carry_trend 0/-1.5/+0.7/+2.5: curves FLAT in the first hours, alpha accrues over days. HL (1h data only 2026-04..11, 226 changes) and live-BN inputs (217, flow incl.) too short: CIs +-6 bp at +1h, +-30 at +24h; flow_bnlive -3.5/-12 at +1/+4h (n.s.). 10 curves.

forms.what: same, by year (2021..2026): is decay speeding up (crowding)? and the cost in bp of executing 1, 2, 4 h late vs on the bar
forms.result: By year, cost of executing late = curve at +k h. 1 h late costs <= 1.3 bp/unit turnover in every BN component (xsmom; others -0.5..+0.6), 4 h late <= 1.2; xsmom's first-hour alpha shrinks 2.4 (2021) -> 1.1 (2025) -> 0.1 (2026): mild decay, not a crowding cliff. At ~110-160 turnover/yr a 1-h-late run every day would cost ~1-2% of the book's alpha per year; the live 4-10 min delay ~0.1-0.2 bp/unit = negligible. Best execution hour not identifiable from a flat curve (E2/E2B said the same about the CME clock). Verdict: late runs harmless for the daily books.

forms.what: live check: actual paper fills of those books (state/paper.db fills) vs the decision bar close: realised delay and its cost; compare with (a)'s curve
forms.result: Live paper fills ('bar' reason, all daily books, 11-09..11-27): BN 1401 fills/17 books/18 days, delay median 13.4 min (p90 15); HL 758/13/19, 11.3 min (p90 33). Signed drift mid-at-fill vs decision close, notional-weighted: BN -3.1 bp (CI -18..+16), HL +10.7 (CI -0.4..+25); by side BN sell +12.8 / buy -13.3, HL sell +14.0 / buy -9.9 = market direction over 18 days, not delay: side-balanced BN -0.3, HL +2.1 bp. Curve (a) predicts ~0.1-0.2 bp at 12 min. Consistent; sample too short to see < 5 bp.

items.reason: Late execution is not a material cost for the daily books: BN 2020-26 decay curves flat (1 h late <= 1.3 bp per unit turnover, 4 h <= 1.2, alpha accrues over 24-48 h, CIs +-1 bp at +1 h, so MDE << 26 bp); live fills 11-13 min late, side-balanced drift -0.3 (BN) / +2.1 (HL) bp. HL/live-BN curves only 7 months (noisy). Best execution hour not identifiable from a flat curve; xsmom first-hour alpha fading 2.4 -> 0.1 bp (2021 -> 2026).

Daily closes under-state intraday troughs

forms.what: same bootstrap with the mean removed (zero edge) and with the mean flipped to -0.5 SR: P(kill within 1 / 2 years) and median time to kill = the switch's power to stop a dead or broken book; compare with the design.md §4 demotion rule (live 60-d Sharpe < 0) as the alternative stop
forms.result: zero edge (demeaned): P(kill) main 37.6 / 71.6 %, main_bn 49.2 / 80.6 % (1 / 2 y; median day 230-340); -0.5 SR: 58-64 / 90-92 % (median day 200-285). Power ~6-7x the false-alarm rate. forms.what: verdict by a general rule (not a book's result): a stop that fires on a real edge more often than on a dead one is mis-set; if so, propose a vol-scaled threshold (k x annual vol) in the backlog for a research session (design change needs its own session); else keep -25 % and write the numbers in design.md's rationale
forms.result: threshold as k x book vol (2 y, real vs zero edge): k .8 38/91-95 %, k 1.0 (= today's 25 %) 15/75-84 %, k 1.25 (~30 %) 4/50-65 %, k 1.5 0.6-0.9/30-46 %. By my pre-stated bar (false alarm > 10 % in 2 y) the fixed 25 % is slightly mis-set, and it is mis-SCALED: at the steady mode's 30 % vol target the same 25 % is k .83 (~35 % false alarms in 2 y). General rule proposed for a research session (design change, not applied here): kill = 1.25 x the book's vol target (31 % at 25 %), plus a per-venue-account guard for main@pair (book-level vol 0.8 % hides -27..-46 % 7-d account swings)

items.reason: measured: the -25 % switch fires on a real edge 11-15 % of the time in 2 y vs 72-84 % on a zero edge (power ~6x); it is a fixed number that should scale with vol (k 1.25 x vol: 4 % false / 50-65 % power); pair book needs a per-account guard. Proposal to backlog for a research session (design.md change rules)
